steps.text: Mix together sugar, oil, soy sauce, green onions, and garlic in a large bowl; set marinade aside.
Cut steak into strips and add to marinade; stir to coat. Cover the bowl and place in the refrigerator, 30 minutes to overnight.
Cook steak with marinade in a wok or frying pan over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until browned, about 5 minutes. Add sesame seeds; cook for 2 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sesame Beef
raw_recipe.description: This sesame beef recipe features strips of round steak marinated with scallions, soy sauce, sugar, and garlic, then stir-fried with sesame seeds.

video.description: Watch how to turn a pound of round steak into a tender and flavorful stir-fry dish. The beef is marinated in soy sauce, sugar, and garlic. Then, it's quickly cooked in a hot wok or a large saute pan. Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds and serve with rice.

review.reviewBody:
This is definitely our favorite stir-fry recipe. I do modify it a little, though, as follows:
 
1. I use stir-fry beef instead of round steak. It comes out much more tender.
2. I double the marinade, but put half in a separate container. This will be the sauce for the stir-fry veggies. 
3. First, I put on the beef with its marinade, and let it cook until done. Then, I remove the beef, and add stir fry veggies and pineapple with the other batch of marinade sauce. Once those are crisp tender, I add the meat back in to warm it up, as well as the sesame seeds, and serve over rice or noodles. 
It's one of my favorite things to eat!!!

I made this in the instant pot. Used the sear function for searing the onion and meat. I dumped everything in on top of the meat & onions. I added the gravy mix, but not the extra water for the mix. Phenomenal. Going in to the rotation.

I followed the measurements as the recipe required, but also made a few personal tweaks. 1st I added 1/2tsp of sesame oil to the marinade.
2nd Before sautéing the beef, I sautéed some sliced mushrooms and thinly sliced carrots & frozen broccoli, then added the beef.
I found the addition of sesame oil was a great addition to the sweetness of the marinade.
Served over brown rice. Viola!!

This is an easy dish to make, but it needed a few changes for me. I followed the recipe the first time I made this - I would probably give it 3 stars - way too sweet as other readers mentioned. The second time I made this, I doubled the sauce ingredients except the sugar - used brown instead of white, and 3 tablespoons olive oil and 1 tablespoon sesame oil instead of the vegetable. Half of this was used for marinade, the other half reserved for later. Added 2 tablespoons cornstarch to the reserved sauce. Stir-fried the meat, removed it from the pan, then stir-fried sliced mushrooms, chopped red pepper, and sliced carrots. Put the meat back in the pan to heat it back up. Then added the sauce and let it thicken up some. Served this over steamed rice with steamed pea pods and asparagus on the side. Awesome! My husband said it tasted like he was at the local Chinese restaurant - but without all the MSG! This will probably be served at my house at least every other week - I love it! Next time, I may make it with a bag of frozen stir-fry veggies.

Great core recipe!
I adjusted the sauce a bit (ratios, this is doubled): 8 tbsp soy sauce, 6 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 3 tbsp brown sugar (add or subtract for desired sweetness) - and mixed it in small blender. this made about 8 oz (4-5 of which i put on the beef to marinade with a small amount of baking soda and about 1/2 tbsp chopped garlic)
added carrots, celery, pea pods, mushrooms, and onions with rice or stir-fry noodles

Hubs and I really enjoyed this, just as we do most stir fries. However, the amount of sugar called for is about four times more than you need – so I did reduce it to just a fourth of what was directed, and used brown sugar rather than white. It was just right. As for the meat, I wanted something more tender than round steak for this quick cooking method so I used sirloin (No Name Steak, to be exact, that I always keep on hand for this very purpose). I also included some good-sized shrimp and, to make this a complete meal, I stir fried some vegetables as well - baby bok choy, mushrooms, bean sprouts and onions. I sprinkled on the toasted sesame seeds and green onion just before serving, in an amount that seemed right to me rather than measuring. What I loved best about this recipe was its simple, clean flavors, not bogged down by lots of different spices or “heat.”

I read a lot of the reviews and it seems everyone did something a little different with this one. I too, made a number of changes as follows: I started with almost a pound of flat iron steak that I cut into thin slices while it was still partially frozen, which made it much easier to slice. I doubled the marinade using half to marinade the steak and the other half to make a sauce after the meat was browned. For the marinade/sauce I cut the sugar in half and used brown sugar instead of white, and used 1 T. sesame oil instead of the vegetable oil. When I was ready to cook, I drained and discarded the marinade from the steak. Then I browned the meat and removed it from the pan. To the hot pan I added the second half of the marinade and added a little cornstarch mixed with water to thicken it. I added the meat back and threw in some extra green onions that I had cut into 1” pieces, covered the skillet and let it simmer a couple of minutes, until the onions had softened. I served this over rice topped with some toasted almonds instead of sesame seeds, and both Hubs and are were very happy. He said “be sure and make this one again!” I guess that says it all. Five stars!

The recipe was amazing and I couldn't be happier with how it turned out. And that's why I made it again a three days later but with a few differences. I used chicken breast instead of beef, cut into large slices, and before marinating I covered the pieces with salt, pepper, and flour. I then marinated the chicken (with the suggested amounts) for about ten minutes, I was in a hurry to make the food and thought it couldn't hurt to take it out before hand. Then I cooked the chicken and for the last ten minutes I added about five small mushrooms cut into slices and a small handful of celery. The sauce thickened nicely, because of the addition of the flour, and the dish went over very well with my family. My cousin actually asked me to make it again soon, and I've been trying for quite some time to find out what she likes. I will definitely look for other stir fry recipes similar to this!

I made this tonight and it's so good. I used 1 1/2 pounds of skirt steak and doubled the sauce. The steak marinated for about 2 hours.

I cooked the steak to a medium rare with the marinade and removed it. I added the second batch (to that I added ginger and sriracha) and cooked asparagus, red bell pepper, snow peas, mushrooms and water chestnuts. I added a slurry of cornstarch and water to thicken the sauce (1/2 cup warm water/1 1/2 tbs cornstarch), put the beef back in and let it warm through. Just a wonderful dish.

I served it with peanut noodles (this site) but rice would be great as well. Plenty of sauce to spoon over. 

This one's a keeper. Loved it.

Loved this! I sliced the beef to make skewers, marinated for an hour and grilled 5 mins on each side over medium direct heat. Doubled the marinade to use as a sauce afterwards, and used sesame oil instead of veg oil. Will make this again and already shared the recipe with family.

I used pre-sliced stir-fry beef from the supercenter. I made double sauce so we could flavor the rice with it. I only used half the sugar, and it was still easily sweet enough. If I had planned ahead, I could add broccoli, carrots, and/or red pepper. Or I like the idea of serving asparagus on the side. Served over white rice I made in the instant pot. Freshly toasted my sesame seeds. It was very good. (Cooked meat, then added and lightly cooked red/green pepper =great!)

I made it 100% as per directions. I wanted to add sesame oil but forgot, will add next time. Soo easy soo good. This makes the perfect recipe as is or add spices to your taste. You can't go wrong here. You can use it s a base to go further
I have been making this recipe for years now. It is one of my go to’s. The toasted sesame oil should not be an option. It is was makes it perfect.
Appears nobody makes it EXACTLY like the recipe 😂. I added a little ginger to the marinade. This is a keeper!
I used exact measurements but substituted maple syrup for sugar. We loved it. First such recipe ever that I consider a keeper. I added mushrooms and sweet onion slices as I sautéed the beef.
Added broccoli and green beans
I made this as written and it was delicious! An absolute keeper! The only thing I did the next time was toast my sesame seeds first before adding them to the meat.
The flavor was delicious. I added fresh green onions when served and next time will double the marinade for a little more juice but otherwise just perfect!
We loved this recipe. I marinated the beef all day. There was plenty of sauce as recipe was written. I did add onions, celery and pea pods. Served over rice. Delicious.

Absolutely delicious! I used beef stew meat instead of round steak so I didn't have to chop it up beforehand. I may be biased because of this, as I looove beef stew meat and think it's hard to go wrong there. But the flavors pair so well together; it's a nice savory weeknight meal that tastes decadent but you don't feel like you're eating too unhealthily. Tastes very good over rice. Will be adding this to the rotation! Quick and easy to make.
